summary: Mount Rainier site of a 1948 frame cabin that replaced the Colonnade lookout; abandoned in the 1960s, destroyed in 1973; a photo caption notes lone wire remains.

events.note: A 1930 report of the National Park Service director mentions a frame lookout station on the ridge above Sunset Park; not stated whether it is this cabin or the Colonnade
Frank Slagle had a summer forest service job at the Sunset lookout station, per a June 20, 1930 Chehalis newspaper item

Destroyed in 1973 after squatters moved in (Willhite and firelookout.com); the Register says removed in 1973

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and firelookout.com say the Colonnade stood two miles southeast of this cabin; Willhite puts it 1,200 feet up the same ridge. Not settled by these sources.
The Register says the cabin was removed in 1973; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in 1973. All three give 1973.
The Register gives 5,530 ft (1,686 m), which matches the brief. Willhite gives 5,560 feet. The story uses the Register figure.

sources.title: Sunset Park Lookout Site - Mt. Rainier National Park

notes_for_editor: Three sources agree on the 1948 build and the 1973 end, but disagree on the Colonnade's distance and the register's 'removed' against the others' 'destroyed'. The 1930 'frame lookout station' is quoted on a hobbyist page and is not placed with certainty at this site; it is reported as unresolved. The only staffing record is the 1930 Chehalis item quoted on the Weebly page. The Mount Rainier National Park lookout history page could not be read (HTTP 503), so no park source is cited. A search snippet mentioned an early-1970s date from Visit Rainier and a 1973 dismantling from a Seattle Times table; neither was read, so neither is used. The brief's record checks out against the Register: county, agency, elevation and the 2012 registration.
